title: An inverse system of nonempty quasi-compact Hausdorff spaces over a directed set has a compatible family of points
statement: Let $K$ be a preordered set in which any two elements have a common upper bound ($K$ may be empty). For every $k\in K$ let $T_k$ be a nonempty topological space which is quasi-compact (every open covering has a finite subcovering) and Hausdorff (any two distinct points have disjoint open neighbourhoods), and for $k\le k'$ let $h_{kk'}:T_{k'}\to T_k$ be a continuous map, with $h_{kk}=\mathrm{id}$ and $h_{kk'}\circ h_{k'k''}=h_{kk''}$ for $k\le k'\le k''$. Then there is a family $(t_k)_{k\in K}$ with $t_k\in T_k$ for every $k$ and $h_{kk'}(t_{k'})=t_k$ for all $k\le k'$.

source.place: Topology, Lemma Tag 0A2R (label lemma-nonempty-limit, line 2507), stated there for a cofiltered index category; here for the cofiltered category $K^{\mathrm{op}}$ of a directed preordered set, with the limit written as the set of compatible families
